key_insight: RE(S) generalizes policy-gradient fine-tuning by updating rollout data every S steps, and still converges globally with an asymptotic Θ(1/T) suboptimality rate while off-policyness can speed escape from weak initial policies.
engineering_relevance: This gives a practical theory for reward-weighted self-training of policies, including LLM post-training, where infrequent rollout refreshes may be both stable and efficient.
method: Model RE(S) as stage-wise optimization over a fixed reward-weighted rollout distribution.
Analyze multi-arm bandits with softmax policies across all S≥1.
Prove global convergence and tight two-sided convergence-rate bounds.
evidence_signal: The paper combines theoretical analysis with numerical experiments on multi-arm bandits to compare convergence behavior across different rollout-update intervals S.
watch_item: The strongest speedup claim depends on initialization and a suitable choice of S, so poorly chosen refresh intervals may still cause long burn-in or delayed improvement.
paper_title: Fine-Tuning on Self-Generated and Reward-Weighted Data: Learning Dynamics, Convergence Rates, and Benefits of Off-Policyness
